title: Formal drift record for FEM-SEC-US@1.2.0 -- three sealed files carry a second, recorded hash

authority.discovery: Orchestrator ENTSCHIED 60 (2026-08-30 01:18): the 1.2.0 seal has been silently broken since 6c2ce83755 (2026-08-09); verifyManifest() is called by nothing in CI.
authority.ruling: Orchestrator ENTSCHIED 63 (2026-08-30 01:35): 'NICHT stummschalten. Drift-Record dokumentiert 1.2.0-Drift UND 1.0.0-Supersede, DANN verifyManifest in CI - Reihenfolge weiter bindend.'
authority.delegation: Standing delegation (verdict + ratification); Karl is informed in the morning report, not asked.

sealReference.manifestUntouchedReason: The manifest bytes are pinned as evidence 'praereg-1.2.0-hash-manifest' in protocol/early-detection/2.0.0/supersede-record.json (sha256 f35a282d..., guarded by tests/studie-stilllegung.test.js). Rewriting the manifest in place would resolve this drift by creating a worse one inside a sealed 2.0.0 record. Append-only wins.

finding.driftSubject: Tag 613: F-25 CI-Heilung -- prep-Gate laeuft auf Linux (Selbsttest ohne OS-Siegel, GQS-Siegel zeilenenden-fest)
finding.elapsedSinceSeal: one day after the seal; undetected for 21 days
finding.rootCause: Blocker A of Tag 613 removed the runtime-lock check from self_test() in scripts/early-detection-confirmatory.py (Karl decision K1a; the real evaluation path still verifies it via authorize_execution -> verify_remote_seal_and_checkpoint -> verify_runtime_lock), and CONFIRMATORY_RUNBOOK.md was updated to match. The commit reasoned explicitly 'hash-manifest.json unveraendert' -- but that reasoning covered the GQS-00 manifest only. The early-detection 1.2.0 manifest, which pins the byte hashes of exactly these two files, was never looked at. Nothing in CI called verifyManifest, so nothing said a word.
finding.substantiveAssessment: The drift is a bookkeeping omission, not a methodology break: the confirmatory evaluation path kept its runtime-lock check, and no preregistration, fixture, threshold or outcome artifact moved. The seal was nevertheless broken, and it stays broken until it is recorded -- which is what this file does.

driftedFiles.reason: Runbook text follows Blocker A: the portable self-test no longer invokes the Windows runtime lock.
Blocker A (Karl decision K1a): self_test() no longer calls verify_runtime_lock(); main() -> authorize_execution() still does.

driftedFiles.movedIn: this record's own change set (ENTSCHIED 63, seal slot 2/3)
driftedFiles.reason: verifyManifest() had to learn to read this record before it could be wired into CI, and the reader necessarily lives in the sealed file it guards. Self-reference acknowledged and bounded: the entry names one exact hash, any other state of this file is red, and the record is a reviewed, committed artifact -- not a runtime switch.

rule: For the files named above and only for them, the acceptedSha256 is a SECOND allowed value beside the sealed hash. Any third state is red. Every file not named here stays nailed to hash-manifest.json. A record that quotes a stale sealedSha256, names an unsealed file, or appears twice in active status makes verifyManifest throw instead of widening the window.
closure: This window does not expire on a date. It closes when FEM-SEC-US gets its next sealed semantic version, whose manifest re-pins these files at one value each; this record then becomes history and status moves to 'closed'. Re-sealing 1.2.0 in place is expressly not the closure path (see sealReference.manifestUntouchedReason).
